Wednesday Oct 14 → Thursday Oct 15, 2026

From a folder of apps to Homeroom

On Wednesday, school lived in a folder on the iPad: Classroom, Gmail, Drive, Docs and the rest, each in its own app. By Thursday night it was one website that plans the week, tracks marks, times study sessions, knows the timetable and even says what to wear.

The build, step by step

Four stops on the way

Beforethe starting point

Where it started

A School folder on the iPad

Gmail, Slides, Docs, Classroom, Drive, Safari and Files, each a separate app, with two more apps blurred out. Every assignment, mark and study session lived somewhere else, or nowhere.

Wed Oct 14246 lines

Step 1

School Hub

The folder became one page you could save to the home screen as a single icon.

246 lines13 KB1 page
  • Greeting and clock that change with the time of day
  • Google search right at the top
  • Six big tiles: Classroom, Gmail, Drive, Docs, Slides and Files
  • New doc and New slides in one tap, plus a dark mode
Wed Oct 142,118 lines

Step 2

Homeroom, the first version

School Hub grew into a real planner with six sections along the bottom. The app tiles moved into their own Apps section.

2,118 lines149 KB6 sections
  • Today: what’s due this week, what’s overdue, your average, your streak and a Next up card
  • Planner: a list and a calendar, class filters, steps inside each assignment, and import from Google Classroom
  • Grades: averages with Ontario levels, Knowledge / Thinking / Communication / Application, what-if marks and “what do I need on the next test”
  • Focus: a timer with 25 / 5, 45 / 10 and 15 / 3 sessions, a 7-day chart, streaks and studying live with friends
  • Coach: homework help from Claude that can read a photo of a worksheet
  • Apps: the School Hub tiles, recent searches and a link to each class in Classroom
Thu Oct 153,212 lines

Step 3 · Finished

The finished website

Homeroom learned your school day: which day of the cycle it is, what class you’re in, when the bell goes, and what the weather means for your outfit.

3,212 lines229 KB7 sections + Closet
  • TimetableNew with the Day 1–5 cycle, rooms, copying a day, and reading your timetable from a photo
  • Live clockNew with a countdown to the next bell
  • Now and nextNew: the class you’re in, the one after, and what’s due for it
  • What to wearNew: an outfit from your own clothes for the forecast, with rain, cold and gym reminders
  • ClosetNew: add clothes from photos, and Claude can pick the outfit
  • Gym days and no-school daysNew (PA days and holidays), so the cycle stays right
  • A break gameNew to play during Focus breaks, and Chat added to Apps
  • Everything from the first version, still there

Where it is now

The website is done. The iPad app came next.

The same week, Homeroom started moving into Swift Playgrounds as a real iPad app. That’s the next chapter.

Open Homeroom

The screens here were re-created from the saved version of each page and filled with a sample student, so every stage shows the same classes and marks. The live website was last saved on Saturday, Oct 17.
